Real estate tip

Choosing a contractor after you buy

Quotes, contracts, permits and payment schedules, and your rights under Ontario law.

Ali Bayat
Figures checked against the sources below on November 21, 2026
Published November 21, 2026
2-minute readHomeownersOntario rules

01Your rights in Ontario

$50+Needs a written contractAny home renovation contract over $50
10 daysTo cancelIf you signed the contract at your home
10%Estimate overrun limitThe final price can't exceed the estimate by more than 10% without your agreement
≤10%Suggested depositOntario recommends no more than 10% up front

02Hiring, step by step

  1. 01

    Get three written quotes

    Week 1

    Same scope for each, so you can compare.

  2. 02

    Check them out

    Week 1–2

    References, the province's Consumer Beware List, WSIB coverage and, for electrical work, an ESA licence.

  3. 03

    Sign a full contract

    Before work starts

    Scope, materials, price with tax, start and finish dates, payment schedule, warranty and cleanup.

  4. 04

    See the permit

    Before work starts

    If they're getting it, see it before construction begins.

  5. 05

    Pay as work is done

    During the job

    Tie payments to finished stages. Never pay in full up front.

03Common scams

  • Door-to-door "good deal"Pressure to sign today, or a free inspection that finds urgent repairs.
  • Big deposit "for materials"Then the contractor disappears.
  • Cash, no paperworkNo contract, no permit, no receipt.
Ali's take

A contractor who won't put it in writing won't stand behind it either. The contract protects both of you.
